I am 55 and have worked this 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My husband spends part of the year working off-farm, so I handle most of the fieldwork myself and I have learned to save labor wherever I can. The winter wheat I sowed last October is already in the ground and greening up, so my focus now is on managing it through to harvest and then getting the maize in quickly.

For the wheat, I will apply a topdressing of urea at the jointing stage and irrigate three times in total—one at green-up or wintering, one at jointing, and one at heading. I put down base fertilizer in the autumn, so across the whole season the crop will get about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium. I will spray twice: once for weeds in early spring and once for aphids or mildew if they appear. I am expecting around 510 kg per mu at harvest in early June.

As soon as the wheat is off the field, I will sow hybrid maize directly into the stubble with no-tillage. That saves me two precious days and keeps the soil moisture, which matters enormously in early June. I will apply 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium, splitting it between sowing and the big trumpet stage. I will irrigate twice—at jointing and at tasseling—because those are the stages that decide yield, and my well water costs electricity so I only use it when the crop truly needs it. I will spray twice as well, for weeds and corn borer. If the summer weather is normal, I should get about 590 kg per mu. My goal is to keep both crops stable without wearing myself out, since I am often working the farm alone.
